overall: Los Angeles is wrapping up a cooler-than-model-expected day, with a running max of 73.9°F established around 13:52 ET (roughly 10:52 PT) — nearly 6 hours ago. Temperature velocity has been flat at +0.0°F/hr since at least 15:00 ET, and afternoon hourly readings have oscillated between 71.6°F and 73.4°F, strongly suggesting the daily peak has already been set. Conditions are markedly cooler than the upper-end GFS/ECMWF guidance, though cloud cover (Beach Hazards Statement, patchy marine layer) and southwest onshore flow appear to be keeping a lid on temperatures.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread was wide today: GFS (75.7°F) and ECMWF (76.3°F) significantly overshot, while HRRR (73.5°F) proved far more accurate and NBM (71.5°F) was too cool. The running max of 73.9°F splits the difference between HRRR and the warmer global models, and intraday observations confirm the HRRR's more conservative solution was correct — a common pattern during marine-layer events in coastal LA.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is almost certainly locked in at 73.9°F, as the running max has been stationary for ~4+ hours with zero velocity and the peak hour occurred mid-morning local time. This places today's TMAX precisely on the boundary between the 72-73F and 74-75F even buckets; the INTRADAY model assigns 97.6% to the 74-75F bucket (likely because 73.9 rounds toward 74°F), but the D1_NOW model favors 72-73F at 59.9%. Given no further warming is expected, the 74-75F even bucket is the edge-case favorite only if the official ASOS TMAX registers at or above 74.0°F — a coin-flip at this margin. Confidence is high that TMAX is 73.9°F; bucket placement is genuinely uncertain at this threshold.
